column7: Consistent with known principles of oncogenic gene regulation, it is well established that structural variations (SVs) can drive cancer progression through a mechanism known as 'enhancer hijacking.' In this process, genomic rearrangements (such as translocations or inversions) reposition distant regulatory elements, particularly highly active super-enhancers, into close spatial proximity with oncogenes, thereby driving their aberrant transcription independently of direct gene copy-number amplification.
column8: This indicates that ERBB2 (HER2) overexpression in breast cancer is not solely dependent on canonical gene amplification, but is also driven by an enhancer hijacking mechanism. These early, clonal translocations repurpose distant breast cancer-specific super-enhancers to aberrantly upregulate ERBB2 transcription, highlighting extragenic structural variants as a distinct, copy-number-independent driver of oncogenesis in this patient population.
